gitCommitNote: This is the source tree commit (Phase 3.8.7.2's own commit) the Phase 3.8.7.3 rebuild was performed against, before Phase 3.8.7.3's own commit (which adds this manifest update) exists. Phase 3.8.7.3 fixes the speech pipeline's genuinely-unbounded backlog and several converging secondary defects (misleading inference-attempted count, status-poll lock contention, a low-severity stale-worker-after-restart race) surfaced by the operator's real Windows report that CIP still became slow/unresponsive during extended listening even after Phase 3.8.7.2's worker-thread fix. See docs/phase-3-8-7-3-live-speech-stability.md.

speechWorkerDecouplingProof.summary: The operator's real Windows report (after Phase 3.8.7.1's model installed successfully) showed app slowness, poor/repetitive transcription, empty Intelligence Feed, and intermittent NO SIGNAL. Root-caused (see docs/phase-3-8-7-2-audit.md) to Whisper inference running synchronously on cpal's real-time audio capture callback thread, blocking both real-time audio servicing and the speech_engine mutex the UI's own 3-second status poll also needed.
speechWorkerDecouplingProof.fix: handle_audio_chunk moved off the audio callback thread onto a dedicated speech worker thread (mirroring the already-proven acoustic-worker pattern), fed via an unbounded channel so the real-time audio callback never blocks or drops a chunk.
speechWorkerDecouplingProof.directBinaryProof: x86_64-w64-mingw32-strings against the extracted cip-desktop.exe finds the mangled symbol for cip_desktop_lib::commands::spawn_speech_worker - direct proof this fix is genuinely compiled into this exact binary, not just present in source.
speechWorkerDecouplingProof.sermonContentCrossDomainFinding: Confirmed, separately, that Sermon/Content/Cross-Domain Intelligence are not wired to the live audio path at all - a pre-existing, already-documented architectural boundary (Phase 3.8's own ServiceReplay screen exists for this reason), not a regression and not fixed this phase.

backpressureProof.summary: The operator's real Windows report after Phase 3.8.7.2's worker-thread fix confirmed genuine improvement (transcription active, audio arriving) but CIP still became slow over extended listening, transcript remained poor/repetitive, and intermittent NO SIGNAL persisted. Re-auditing the actual current code (docs/phase-3-8-7-3-audit.md) confirmed the operator's own hypothesis: the speech channel (`mpsc::channel::<AudioChunk>()`, start_listening) was genuinely unbounded - if Whisper inference ever takes longer than the ~3s of audio each inference window represents, the backlog grows without limit, and the worker falls permanently further behind live audio.
backpressureProof.fix: A shared `pending_ms: Arc<AtomicU64>` tracks the wall-clock duration of audio queued but not yet fed to the engine (milliseconds, not raw chunk count, since chunk size/rate varies by capture device). start_listening's sink closure increments it on send; spawn_speech_worker decrements it on dequeue. When the remaining backlog crosses OVERLOAD_THRESHOLD_MS (10s), the worker drains and discards the entire queued backlog plus WhisperSpeechEngine's own internal buffer (new SpeechEngine::discard_buffered_audio() trait method) rather than grinding through an ever-more-stale FIFO - this was chosen over a plain bounded/drop-newest channel specifically because that design would still leave the worker permanently behind, never catching up to live audio.
backpressureProof.secondaryFixes: (1) The inferences-attempted counter previously counted every feed_audio call to a ready engine, not just the ~1-in-300 that actually trigger a real whisper.cpp inference pass - fixed via a new SpeechEngine::last_feed_triggered_inference() trait method, checked after each feed_audio call. (2) All four status-poll call sites (get_pilot_diagnostics, start_listening, stop_listening, get_live_status) locked speech_engine's mutex just to read is_ready() - the same mutex the worker holds for the full duration of a blocking Whisper inference - fixed by caching the fact once at construction (AppState::speech_ready), which never changes after that for either existing engine. (3) A low-severity race where a speech worker whose channel closed mid-inference could write output into a newer listening session after a rapid stop/start - fixed via a listening_generation counter checked before any non-empty result is emitted/persisted.
backpressureProof.newDiagnostics: SpeechRuntimeDiagnostics gained queuePendingMs, queueHighWaterMs, overloadEvents, audioMsDroppedOverload, lastInferenceDurationMs/maxInferenceDurationMs/avgInferenceDurationMs, lastTranscriptPipelineDurationMs, and a derived overloadState (normal/busy/falling_behind/overloaded) - all surfaced in the System Diagnostics panel's new 'Speech pipeline health' section, so the operator can directly answer whether audio is backing up, whether inference is keeping up, and whether the app is actively shedding stale audio.
backpressureProof.directBinaryProof: x86_64-w64-mingw32-strings against the extracted cip-desktop.exe finds the mangled symbols for cip_desktop_lib::commands::spawn_speech_worker, cip_desktop_lib::commands::handle_audio_chunk, cip_desktop_lib::commands::saturating_sub_u64, and both new SpeechEngine trait method overrides (WhisperSpeechEngine's discard_buffered_audio/last_feed_triggered_inference) - direct proof this phase's fix is genuinely compiled into this exact binary. classify_overload/chunk_duration_ms (small pure functions) were inlined by the release-mode optimizer, as expected, and are instead verified via 10 dedicated unit tests run as part of this phase's regression suite.
backpressureProof.notImplementedThisPhase: Extended-overload (Test C) and stop-during-inference (Test E) real-thread integration scenarios could not be exercised via automated test in this container - consistent with this codebase's own established testing boundary (commands.rs's test module: command tests stop short of standing up a full tauri::test::mock_builder() harness). These require the operator's own real-hardware 20-30 minute long-run test.

provenance.builtDuring: Phase 3.8.6 (Windows Whisper Build & Packaging Audit) - the operator's Phase 3.8.5 real-Windows re-test confirmed audio capture now genuinely works (SIGNAL CAPTURED, correct listening lifecycle) but isolated the remaining blocker to transcription itself ('SPEECH ERROR'). The audit (docs/phase-3-8-6-audit.md) confirmed the root cause the operator suspected: no Windows build in this project's history has ever been compiled with the `whisper` Cargo feature, so no prior installer could ever transcribe regardless of hardware. Compiling with --features whisper for this exact cross-compilation target (x86_64-pc-windows-gnu, from Linux) hit two independent, real, verified toolchain/upstream defects that had to be fixed before a working build was even possible: (1) whisper.cpp's vendored `ggml` CMake build unconditionally strips the 'lib' prefix from its own static library output for any Windows target (assuming MSVC naming), but the actual linker here is MinGW's GNU ld, which requires the Unix 'libX.a' convention for a plain -lX flag - so ggml.a/ggml-base.a/ggml-cpu.a were built but never found; (2) this container's default x86_64-w64-mingw32-gcc/g++ alternative is the win32-threading-model variant, but whisper.cpp/ggml link against pthread and expect POSIX threading, producing 'undefined reference to __mingwthr_key_dtor' at final link - fixed by switching to the already-installed posix-threads alternative via update-alternatives. Neither fix touches the vendored whisper-rs-sys/ggml/whisper.cpp source; see scripts/build-windows-whisper.sh for the exact, repeatable two-pass build process and docs/phase-3-8-6-windows-whisper-build.md for full root-cause evidence. Separately, the audit also found and fixed a real, previously-undocumented defect that would have blocked correct transcription even with the feature/model both present: `integrations/audio` delivers AudioChunks at the capture device's own native sample rate and never resamples (by design - see its module docs), but WhisperSpeechEngine hardcoded a 16kHz assumption and the one consumer that needed to convert (handle_audio_chunk) never did - so a real Windows device negotiating 44.1kHz/48kHz (the norm for consumer WASAPI devices like Stereo Mix/Microphone Array) would have fed audio to Whisper at roughly 3x the wrong rate. Fixed by adding SpeechEngine::required_sample_rate_hz() (a new default trait method, Some(16_000) only for WhisperSpeechEngine) and a linear-interpolation resampler at the one call site that needs it. Also fixed: the real underlying model-load/inference error text (already computed by WhisperSpeechEngine and SpeechEngineError, but discarded after logging) is now retained in AppState and surfaced through the existing get_pilot_diagnostics command/System Diagnostics panel (feature compiled, model loaded, chunks received, last chunk sample rate, inferences attempted/succeeded, real last-error text) instead of the generic 'SPEECH ERROR' notice alone.
provenance.buildEnvironment: cross-compiled from Linux using rustup target x86_64-pc-windows-gnu, gcc-mingw-w64 (posix-threads alternative - see whisperFeatureProof above), cmake, and nsis (makensis) via `npx tauri build --target x86_64-pc-windows-gnu --features whisper` after the two build.rs-external fixes described above; see scripts/build-windows-whisper.sh for the exact repeatable process

releaseCandidateStatement: This is the Phase 3.8.7.3 SOFTWARE RELEASE CANDIDATE for Windows x64 (Live Speech Stability, Instrumentation & Backpressure) - the first Windows installer in this project's history where the speech pipeline's backlog is measured and bounded rather than allowed to grow without limit, on top of the worker-thread decoupling (Phase 3.8.7.2), the model-provisioning feature (Phase 3.8.7.1), the DLL-bundling fix (Phase 3.8.6.1), and the whisper-feature build (Phase 3.8.6), all still verified working in this exact artifact. It is a real, verifiable build artifact - not a placeholder, not a simulation, not a fabrication - and every claim in this manifest is backed by direct inspection of this exact packaged .exe, including the compiled-in spawn_speech_worker/handle_audio_chunk/saturating_sub_u64/discard_buffered_audio/last_feed_triggered_inference symbols (see backpressureProof, speechWorkerDecouplingProof, modelProvisioningProof, runtimeDependencyProof, whisperFeatureProof above). See docs/phase-3-8-7-3-live-speech-stability.md for the full breakdown and final gate.
modelPackagingStatement: NO Whisper model file is bundled with this installer, and none could be obtained to bundle: this container's egress policy blocks the standard model host (huggingface.co), and no ggml/gguf model file exists anywhere in this repository to embed even if bundling logic were added. An in-app 'Select Existing Model File' button (native file picker + install_whisper_model command, Phase 3.8.7.1) validates a candidate file by actually loading it as a real Whisper model before installing it atomically - the operator downloads the canonical file themselves (their own Windows machine's internet access, not this container's) and installs it with one click. No automatic download and no network dependency were added to the SHIPPED APPLICATION itself - the app never initiates any network request. See modelProvisioningProof and pilot-evidence/3.8.7.1/build/model-provisioning-evidence.json for the full reasoning.
physicalHardwareStatement: CONFIRMED on real Windows hardware by the operator for the Phase 3.8.7.2 artifact (worker-thread decoupling produced genuine, partial improvement - the operator's own real report driving this phase). This exact THIS artifact (SHA-256 78ecdf79...) - the backpressure/instrumentation rebuild - has NOT yet been installed or launched on real Windows hardware. It has been verified at Environment A only: full regression suite green (Rust default/whisper features including 10 new backpressure unit tests, frontend typecheck/lint/test/build all green), the packaged installer directly extracted and inspected (DLLs still present, whisper feature symbols present, file-picker plugin symbols present, and - directly proving this phase's fix - the spawn_speech_worker/handle_audio_chunk/saturating_sub_u64/discard_buffered_audio/last_feed_triggered_inference symbols compiled into the binary). The decisive next step remains the operator's own real-hardware long-run test (20-30 minutes, periodically checking Diagnostics' new 'Speech pipeline health' section for queue depth/high-water mark/overload events/inference duration/worker lag, then Stop Listening and restart): does CIP remain responsive the entire time, does queue depth stay bounded (never growing unbounded even if inference briefly falls behind), does the app clearly show BUSY/FALLING BEHIND/OVERLOADED states rather than silently degrading, and does it recover cleanly after an overload episode.
githubReleaseStatus: NOT CONFIGURED - no .github/workflows directory exists in this repository, and no GitHub Release has been created for this artifact. This installer is available only via this repository's working tree (release/windows/), not via GitHub Releases or any CI/CD pipeline.
obtainingWithoutDeveloperTooling: The file at release/windows/Church Intelligence Platform_0.1.0_x64-setup.exe can be copied/transferred directly (e.g. via a git clone of this repository, a direct file download, or a USB drive) to the target Windows machine and run there. Running the installer on Windows requires none of: Claude Code, Rust, Cargo, Node.js, npm, or the CIP source tree - only the .exe file itself. A real Whisper model file (see modelPackagingStatement) must be placed separately by the operator for transcription to work.
knownLimitations: UNSIGNED release candidate - Windows SmartScreen will show an 'unknown publisher' warning on first run

This exact rebuilt artifact has NOT yet been installed or launched on real Windows hardware - Environment A (automated build-time verification, including compiled-in symbol checks for this phase's fixes) only. The operator's own real-hardware 20-30 minute long-run re-test is the decisive, pending gate - see physicalHardwareStatement.

The overload-drain backpressure strategy is measured/reasoned from real hardware evidence (the operator's own 480-sample/48kHz chunk rate) but its extended-overload and stop-during-inference behavior (Long-Run Tests C and E) could not be exercised via automated real-thread test in this container - only via the pure-function unit tests for the classification/duration logic (Tests A/B/D). Sermon/Content/Cross-Domain Intelligence are NOT wired to the live audio path - only Bible Intelligence and (separately) acoustic Music recognition are. This is a pre-existing, already-documented architectural boundary (Phase 3.8's own ServiceReplay screen exists for this reason), confirmed again this phase but deliberately NOT changed.

This phase's fix bounds the speech pipeline's backlog and surfaces its real timing - it does not change whisper.cpp/tiny.en's inherent transcription accuracy, real background noise, or Stereo Mix audio characteristics. 'CIP stays responsive and never grows unbounded memory,' not 'perfect transcription,' is the honest bar for the operator's next real-hardware test.
